title.es: La historia antes de la historia

es: Reconocer qué acción ocurrió primero cuando un relato combina past perfect y past simple.

teaching.en: When we arrived at the station, the train had already left.
teaching.es: Cuando llegamos a la estación, el tren ya se había ido.
teaching.explanationEs: Had + participio (left) es lo que pasó primero; arrived ocurrió después.
segments: When we arrived at the station,
the train had already left.
teaching.audioText: When we arrived at the station, the train had already left.

teaching.en: Grandma told an anecdote about her wedding: she had lost her ring the night before.
teaching.es: La abuela contó una anécdota de su boda: había perdido el anillo la noche anterior.
teaching.explanationEs: Told va en pasado simple; had lost marca lo que ya había ocurrido antes de la boda.
segments: Grandma told an anecdote about her wedding: she
had lost her ring the night before.
teaching.audioText: Grandma told an anecdote about her wedding: she had lost her ring the night before.

teaching.en: The last guest had left before Grandpa found the ring under the table.
teaching.es: El último invitado se había ido antes de que el abuelo encontrara el anillo debajo de la mesa.
teaching.explanationEs: Had left pasó antes que found: el orden de los hechos no es el orden de la frase.
segments: The last guest had left before Grandpa
found the ring under the table.
teaching.audioText: The last guest had left before Grandpa found the ring under the table.

teaching.en: It was a big surprise because nobody had told Ana about the party.
teaching.es: Fue una gran sorpresa porque nadie le había dicho a Ana lo de la fiesta.
teaching.explanationEs: Nobody had told = nadie había dicho: explica la causa de la sorpresa.
segments: It was a big surprise because nobody
had told Ana about the party.
teaching.audioText: It was a big surprise because nobody had told Ana about the party.

teaching.en: Earlier that day, it had rained, so the garden was wet.
teaching.es: Más temprano ese día había llovido, así que el jardín estaba mojado.
teaching.explanationEs: Había llovido antes del momento del que hablas; was wet describe ese momento.
segments: Earlier that day, it had rained,
so the garden was wet.
teaching.audioText: Earlier that day, it had rained, so the garden was wet.

es: Elegir entre past perfect y past simple con already, just, never before y by the time.

teaching.en: By the time we got to the concert, the band had already started.

concert, the band had already started.

teaching.en: When Ana's phone rang, Leo left the house.

Leo left the house.
teaching.audioText: When Ana's phone rang, Leo left the house.

teaching.en: When Ana's phone rang, Leo had already left the house.

segments: When Ana's phone rang, Leo
had already left the house.
teaching.audioText: When Ana's phone rang, Leo had already left the house.

teaching.en: Mia had just finished her homework when her friend arrived.

teaching.audioText: Mia had just finished her homework when her friend arrived.

played that song at a concert before.

teaching.en: There was a misunderstanding: I thought you had forgotten the plan.
teaching.es: Hubo un malentendido: pensé que habías olvidado el plan.
teaching.explanationEs: Thought + had + participio: lo que creías que ya había pasado.

teaching.en: I apologise: I had not read your message before the meeting.
teaching.es: Me disculpo: no había leído tu mensaje antes de la reunión.
teaching.explanationEs: Had not + participio: algo que todavía no había pasado.
segments: I apologise: I had not read

teaching.audioText: I apologise: I had not read your message before the meeting.

teaching.en: I had not forgotten the plan; my phone had stopped working.
teaching.es: No había olvidado el plan; mi teléfono había dejado de funcionar.
teaching.explanationEs: Had + participio explica la verdadera causa del malentendido.
segments: I had not forgotten the plan;
my phone had stopped working.
teaching.audioText: I had not forgotten the plan; my phone had stopped working.

teaching.en: I suggest we meet on Saturday instead.
teaching.es: Propongo que quedemos el sábado en su lugar.
teaching.explanationEs: Suggest + sujeto + verbo base: sin to ni -ing; instead = en su lugar.

teaching.en: Sara thought I had cancelled the plan, but I had only moved it to Sunday.
teaching.es: Sara pensó que yo había cancelado el plan, pero solo lo había pasado al domingo.
teaching.explanationEs: Dos past perfect seguidos: lo que ella creía y lo que realmente había pasado.

prompt.es: Elige la frase: «Pensé que habías olvidado el plan.»

choices.text: I thought you have forgotten the plan.
I thought you had forget the plan.
I thought you had forgotten the plan.

feedback.es: Lo que creías que ya había pasado va con had + participio (forgotten); las otras formas son incorrectas.

hint.es: Lo que creías que ya había pasado va en had + participio.

prompt.es: Completa: «Lo siento. No había leído tu mensaje antes de la reunión.»

answer.text: not

feedback.es: Had not + participio expresa que algo todavía no había ocurrido antes de la reunión.

hint.es: Es la palabra que niega a had.

origin.text: I am sorry. I had ___ read your message before the meeting.

prompt.es: Ordena: «¿Quedamos mejor el sábado?»

answer.text: Shall we meet on Saturday instead

feedback.es: Shall we + verbo base propone un plan; instead indica que es en lugar de otra fecha.

hint.es: Empieza con Shall we y termina con instead.

prompt.es: Escucha a Sara y elige por qué vino un día equivocado.

choices.text: She had noted the wrong day.

feedback.es: Sara explica que había escrito el día equivocado en su móvil; por eso vino el viernes.

origin.audio: I am sorry, Tom. I had written the wrong day in my phone, so I came on Friday instead of Saturday.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada frase con su función.

pairs: I had not seen your message.

pairs.es: explicar lo que no había pasado

feedback.es: Aclarar un malentendido combina cuatro funciones: lo que creías, lo que había pasado, la disculpa y la propuesta.

pairs: I had not seen your message.

pairs.es: explicar lo que no había pasado

prompt.es: Completa: «Pensé que habías perdido el autobús. Propongo que quedemos el domingo.»

answer.text: thought | meet

feedback.es: Thought + had + participio dice lo que creías; suggest + we + verbo base propone otra fecha.

sentences: I ___ you had missed the bus.
I suggest we ___ on Sunday instead.

prompt.es: Según el mensaje de Ana, ¿por qué no fue al cine?

choices.text: She had gone to another cinema.

feedback.es: Ana dice que había ido al cine equivocado; no dice que olvidara el plan ni que perdiera la entrada.

origin.text: Leo: I waited at the cinema, but you did not come. Ana: I am sorry. I had gone to the wrong cinema, so I did not see you there. Shall we go on Sunday instead?

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué había pasado cuando vio el mensaje.

feedback.es: «The film had already started» es lo que había pasado cuando vio el mensaje; después se fue a casa.

origin.audio: By the time I saw your message, the film had already started, so I went home. I am very sorry.

prompt.es: Escribe tu respuesta a Leo: explica, discúlpate y propón otra fecha.

answer.text: I am so sorry, Leo. I had not forgotten the plan. My phone had broken, so I had not seen your message before I left home. I did not know that you had waited for an hour. Shall we meet on Saturday instead?
accepted: I am so sorry, Leo. I had not forgotten the plan. My phone had broken, so I had not seen your message before I left home. I did not know that you had waited for an hour. Shall we meet on Saturday instead?
I apologise, Leo. I had not forgotten the plan, but my phone had stopped working, so I had not read your message. I am sorry you waited for an hour. I suggest we meet on Saturday instead.
Sorry, Leo. I had not seen your message because my phone had broken, and I had not forgotten the plan. I know you had waited for an hour. How about Saturday?

feedback.es: Una buena aclaración explica lo anterior con dos had (not) + participio, se disculpa y propone otra fecha.

origin.text: Situación: Leo te esperó una hora en el parque y piensa que olvidaste el plan. En realidad, tu móvil se había roto y no habías visto su mensaje. Escribe tu respuesta: explica lo que había pasado, discúlpate y propón quedar el sábado.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Pensé que habías cancelado el plan.»

answer.text: I thought you had cancelled the plan

feedback.es: I thought + had cancelled expresa lo que creías que ya había pasado con el plan.

prompt.es: ¿Qué frase sirve para disculparse y dar la causa?

choices.text: I am sorry, I had not seen your message.
I am sorry, I not had seen your message.
I am sorry, I had not see your message.

feedback.es: Had not va junto y después el participio seen; las otras opciones cambian el orden o usan el verbo base.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué propone la hablante.

choices.text: Going to the concert next week.

feedback.es: Con «Shall we go next week?» la hablante propone ir la semana siguiente, ya aclarado el malentendido.

origin.audio: Hello, Mia. I thought you had lost the concert tickets, but your sister told me about your fever. Shall we go next week?

prompt.es: Completa: «Lo siento, no había contestado tu llamada.»

answer.text: answered

feedback.es: Had not + answered: en ese momento todavía no había contestado la llamada.

origin.text: I am sorry. I had not ___ your call.
